title: National Fellowship Scheme for Scheduled Tribes
body_text:
Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed in Lok Sabha today that Under the scheme of National Fellowship Scheme for Scheduled Tribes (NFST) a total of 3750 number of fellowships awarded during the last five years. Details of courses covered, institutions in which the scholars were enrolled in West Bengal on district wise and year-wise are given at Annexure-I .
National Fellowship Scheme for Scheduled Tribes (NFST) , being a Central Sector Scheme, has no provision regarding allocation of State-wise budget. Details of actual disbursement made in the State of West Bengal, district-wise, during last five years is at Annexure-II .
Under the National Fellowship for ST students’ scheme, online portal for inviting applications generally opens on 1st July and closes on 30th September of the academic year. Thereafter, verification of applications is carried out and further merit list of 750 selected candidates are uploaded on the Ministry's website. Subsequently, the release of fellowship funds is processed, subject to completion of necessary compliance by students such as submission of joining report, linking of bank account, continuation certificate etc. and also the availability of funds under the budget head of the scheme.
Complaints/grievances relating to the scholarship schemes (including NFST Scheme) are generally received through the CPGRAMS/PG Portal and all grievances are disposed of within the prescribed timeline. The average disposal time of grievances received in CPGRAMS during 01/04/2021 to 31/03/2026 is given below: -
CPGRAMS/PG Portal Report for all scholarship Grievances (including NFST scheme) Number of grievance brought forward Number of grievance(s) received Number of grievance(s) disposed Average disposal time (Days) 1 1680 1681 7
Under the scheme of National Fellowship Scheme for Scheduled Tribes (NFST) a total of 2250 number of fellowships awarded during the last three years. The number of scholars completing their courses/research during the last three years is indicated in the table below.
Financial Year No of Students completing Research* 2023-24 294 2024-25 156 2025-26 226
* 750 fellowships are given every year for a period of 5 years.
The constant support from Ministry of Tribal Affairs to 750 fresh fellowship every year is ensuring representation of Scheduled Tribe scholars in higher education and research.

enrichment.summary: In a Lok Sabha reply, the Union Minister of State for Tribal Affairs stated that 3,750 fellowships were awarded under the National Fellowship Scheme for Scheduled Tribes (NFST) over the last five years, with 750 fresh fellowships sanctioned annually for five-year research programmes. The scheme is a Central Sector Scheme with no state-wise budget allocation, and applications are invited online each year from 1 July to 30 September. Data was also shared on scholars completing research (294 in 2023-24, 156 in 2024-25, 226 in 2025-26) and on grievance redressal via CPGRAMS, which recorded 1,681 grievances disposed of with an average disposal time of 7 days between April 2021 and March 2026.
enrichment.context:
The National Fellowship Scheme for Scheduled Tribes (NFST) is administered by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs to support ST students pursuing higher research (M.Phil/Ph.D) by providing financial assistance similar to UGC fellowships, aiming to improve representation of Scheduled Tribes in higher education and academia. It is part of a broader family of central fellowship schemes for marginalized groups, including the National Fellowship for OBCs and similar schemes for SCs, reflecting the government's affirmative action framework rooted in Articles 15(4), 16(4), and 46 of the Constitution, which mandate special provisions for the educational and economic advancement of Scheduled Tribes and other weaker sections.

Being a Central Sector Scheme, NFST is fully funded by the Centre without a state-wise budget split, meaning allocation to states like West Bengal depends on actual applications and selections rather than a pre-fixed quota. Timely redressal of grievances (via CPGRAMS) related to scholarship disbursement is also significant in the context of ease of access to welfare benefits and the digitization of governance, an important theme in India's push toward transparent and accountable welfare delivery.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the National Fellowship Scheme for Scheduled Tribes (NFST):
1. It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with state-wise budget allocation.
2. Under the scheme, 750 fresh fellowships are awarded every year for a period of five years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, NFST is a Central Sector Scheme (not Centrally Sponsored) with no provision for state-wise budget allocation, so statement 1 is incorrect. Statement 2 is correct, as 750 fresh fellowships are awarded annually for a five-year period.

prelims_questions.question: The National Fellowship Scheme for Scheduled Tribes (NFST) falls under the administrative purview of which Ministry?
options: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
prelims_questions.explanation: NFST is administered by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, as confirmed by the Lok Sabha reply given by its Minister of State.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of fellowship schemes like the National Fellowship Scheme for Scheduled Tribes (NFST) in promoting higher education and research among socially disadvantaged groups in India. What challenges persist in ensuring their effective implementation?
